title: Practice 2: Two verbs for every way of going

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Когда вы ___ (ехать — to go by vehicle, ride, one way) в Йорк?
exercises.why: The expression "to go by …" (means of transportation) is rendered in Russian by на + prepositional case: ехать на поезде (на автобусе, на автомобиле), лететь на самолёте. — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: When are you going to York?
exercises.context: The expression "to go by …" (means of transportation) is rendered in Russian by на + prepositional case: ехать на поезде (на автобусе, на автомобиле), лететь на самолёте.

exercises.q: Вы все так разоделись. Куда ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way)?

exercises.q: Синеватая птица ___ (лететь — to fly, one way) к высокому дереву.
exercises.why: Капитан летит в Вашингтон.* The verb идти means "to go, be going". It refers to going on foot. This verb belongs to the 1st conjugation (characterized by the vowel -ё-, like живу, -ёшь, -ёт …). The verb ехать refers to going by some means of transportation, i.e. riding, driving: Я еду на поезде. (Я иду пешком.) Я еду в Европу. (Я иду в комнату.) This verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation. Note. — The motion of a vehicle is expressed by идёт (not едет) when time-table and regular route are involved: Куда идёт этот автобус?* — DLI, Lesson 22.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: A bluish bird is flying to the tall tree.
exercises.context: Капитан летит в Вашингтон.
